title: Auditing Reward Hackability in Code RL Training Environments
abstract: arXiv:2606.16062v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Code RL rewards a policy for passing a task's tests, so a test suite that accepts a wrong patch trains the wrong behavior. We measure how often open code RL environments accept wrong patches and how reliably hackable tasks can be detected and repaired, checking each claim by execution against the task's gold patch. First, 22.4% of 49 SWE-bench Verified tasks accept a Docker-verified patch that behaves differently from the gold patch, and 57.8% against a stronger attacker. The gold-patch check is necessary: an attacker not shown the gold patch returns it for 31% of its passing "exploits". Second, across 134 public SWE-bench submissions, models pass hackable tasks 28.6 pp more often than tasks of the same difficulty, mostly because those tasks are passable at all; pooled over three attacker runs, hackable tasks still exceed matched passable ones (p = 0.014). Third, repair is harder to verify than detection: 61.9% of LLM-written repair

translated_title: 审计代码强化学习训练环境中的奖励可作弊性
translated_abstract: 代码强化学习根据策略是否通过任务的测试来给予奖励，因此一个会接受错误补丁的测试套件就会训练出错误的行为。我们测量了开源代码RL环境接受错误补丁的频率，以及可作弊任务被检测和修复的可靠性，并通过将每个补丁与任务的标准补丁进行执行对比来验证所有结论。首先，在49个SWE-bench Verified任务中，22.4%的任务会接受一个经Docker验证但与标准补丁行为不同的补丁，面对更强的攻击者时这一比例达57.8%。标准补丁检查是必要的：未被告知标准补丁的攻击者在其通过的“漏洞利用”中有31%实际上返回的就是标准补丁本身。其次，在134个公开的SWE-bench提交中，模型通过可作弊任务的频率比同等难度的任务高出28.6个百分点，这主要源于这些任务本身是可以通过的；在三次攻击者运行汇总来看，可作弊任务的通过率仍显著超过匹配的可完成任务（p = 0.014）。第三，修复比检测更难验证：61.9%由LLM编写的修复补丁……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文通过基于标准补丁的执行验证系统审计了代码强化学习训练环境的奖励作弊问题，发现约22.4%（强攻击者下57.8%）的SWE-bench Verified任务会接受错误补丁，且模型在这些可作弊任务上的通过率显著更高，凸显了对RL训练环境进行作弊检测与修复审计的必要性。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically audits reward hackability in code RL training environments using gold-patch-based execution checks, finding that 22.4% (57.8% under stronger attacks) of SWE-bench Verified tasks accept wrong patches and that models pass hackable tasks significantly more often, highlighting the need for auditing detection and repair in RL training environments.
